chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from a man, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

We went to him as a group and said, 'O son of the Messenger of Allah! We intend to go to Iraq, so advise us.' Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Let your strong ones strengthen your weak ones, and let your rich ones assist your poor ones, and do not divulge our secret nor broadcast our matter. And whenever a hadith comes to you from us, and you find a witness or two witnesses for it from the Book of Allah, then take it; otherwise, pause with it, then refer it back to us until it becomes clear to you.'

And know that the one awaiting this matter has a reward like that of the fasting one who stands (in night prayer). And whoever catches up with our Qa'im and goes out with him and kills our enemy, for him is a reward like that of twenty martyrs. And whoever is killed with our Qa'im, for him is a reward like that of twenty-five martyrs.

key_terms.الْمُنْتَظِرُ: The one awaiting (the reappearance of the Imam)

ai.seo_question: What are the rewards for those who await the Qa'im and fight with him according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi’s chapter on Occultation, this hadith outlines the protocol for the Shia community during the Minor and Major Ghaybah, emphasizing communal solidarity, preserving the secret of the Imam, and verifying reports against the Quran. It further underscores the eschatological significance of 'Intizar' (awaiting), equating the patience of those waiting for the Qa'im with the reward of continuous fasting and prayer.
